accepted.s: Which ruler shifted the capital of the Vijayanagara kingdom from Anegondi to Vijayanagara?
accepted.x: Harihara I shifted the capital from Anegondi to Vijayanagara.
accepted.tq: Direct ruler–achievement recall.
accepted.sec: Sangama rulers → achievement (Harihara I, Bukka I, Harihara II, Devaraya I, Devaraya II)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Harihara I:
1. He annexed the Hoysala kingdom in 1346.
2. He annexed the Kadamba territory in 1347.
3. He took Udayagiri himself in 1343.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Harihara I annexed the Hoysala kingdom in 1346 and the Kadambas in 1347. Udayagiri was taken by Bukka, not Harihara I, in 1343.
accepted.tq: Separate the ruler from the achievement attributed to his associate.
accepted.sec: Sangama rulers → achievement (Harihara I, Bukka I, Harihara II, Devaraya I, Devaraya II)

accepted.s: The title ‘Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati’ was assumed by which Vijayanagara ruler?
accepted.x: Harihara I bore the title ‘Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati’.
accepted.tq: Direct title–ruler matching.
accepted.sec: Sangama rulers → achievement (Harihara I, Bukka I, Harihara II, Devaraya I, Devaraya II)

accepted.s: Who took Udayagiri in 1343 according to the record of the early Sangama rulers?
accepted.x: Bukka took Udayagiri in 1343.
accepted.tq: Use the associated person rather than the principal ruler in a date-based fact.
accepted.sec: Sangama rulers → achievement (Harihara I, Bukka I, Harihara II, Devaraya I, Devaraya II)

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Devaraya I ruled from 1406 to 1422. The period 1422–1446 belongs to Devaraya II.
accepted.tq: Check the reign-period pair before accepting the familiar ruler name.
accepted.sec: Sangama rulers → achievement (Harihara I, Bukka I, Harihara II, Devaraya I, Devaraya II)

accepted.s:
Bukka I is associated with which combination of achievements?
1. Completion of the city of Vijayanagara
2. Conquest of Madurai
3. Reconciliation of Jains and Vaishnavas
4. Construction of the Ganigitti Jain temple
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Bukka I completed the city, conquered Madurai and reconciled Jains and Vaishnavas. The Ganigitti Jain temple was built by Irugappa, minister of Harihara II.
accepted.tq: Identify the one achievement shifted from one Sangama ruler to another.
accepted.sec: Sangama rulers → achievement (Harihara I, Bukka I, Harihara II, Devaraya I, Devaraya II)

accepted.s: Which Sangama ruler was the longest-reigning king of the dynasty?
accepted.x: Harihara II, who ruled from 1377 to 1404, was the longest-reigning Sangama king.
accepted.tq: Direct comparison within a ruling dynasty.
accepted.sec: Sangama rulers → achievement (Harihara I, Bukka I, Harihara II, Devaraya I, Devaraya II)

accepted.s:
Harihara II is associated with which of the following titles?
1. Rajavyasa
2. Rajavalmiki
3. Gajabetekara
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Harihara II bore the titles Rajavyasa and Rajavalmiki. Gajabetekara was a title of Devaraya II.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between titles of successive rulers.
accepted.sec: Sangama rulers → achievement (Harihara I, Bukka I, Harihara II, Devaraya I, Devaraya II)

accepted.s: The famine known as ‘Durgadevi Karamu’ occurred during the reign of which ruler?
accepted.x: The famine called ‘Durgadevi Karamu’ is associated with the reign of Harihara II.
accepted.tq: Direct event–ruler association.
accepted.sec: Sangama rulers → achievement (Harihara I, Bukka I, Harihara II, Devaraya I, Devaraya II)

accepted.s: Who built the Ganigitti Jain temple and wrote the Navaratnamala?
accepted.x: Irugappa, the minister of Harihara II, built the Ganigitti Jain temple and wrote Navaratnamala.
accepted.tq: Match the minister with both his architectural and literary work.
accepted.sec: Sangama rulers → achievement (Harihara I, Bukka I, Harihara II, Devaraya I, Devaraya II)

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Devaraya I — Dam across the Tungabhadra
2. Devaraya I — War with Firuz Shah
3. Devaraya I — First recruitment of Muslims into the army
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Devaraya I built a dam and canals, fought Firuz Shah and is recorded as the first Sangama ruler to recruit Muslims into the army.
accepted.tq: Combine several achievements of one ruler before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: Sangama rulers → achievement (Harihara I, Bukka I, Harihara II, Devaraya I, Devaraya II)

accepted.s:
Arrange the following rulers in chronological order of their accession:
A. Harihara II
B. Bukka I
C. Devaraya II
D. Devaraya I
accepted.x: Bukka I succeeded Harihara I, followed by Harihara II, Devaraya I and Devaraya II.
accepted.tq: Use the accession sequence of the Sangama rulers.
accepted.sec: Sangama rulers → achievement (Harihara I, Bukka I, Harihara II, Devaraya I, Devaraya II)

accepted.s: Who led the conquest of Madurai during the reign of Bukka I?
accepted.x: Kumara Kampana, son of Bukka I, overthrew Sambhuvaraya in 1366 and destroyed the Madurai Sultanate.
accepted.tq: Direct identification of the commander in a dynastic conquest.
accepted.sec: Bukka I - southern conquest and its literary record (author), foreign embassy

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kumara Kampana overthrew Sambhuvaraya in 1366.
2. Saluva Mangu killed the Sultan of Madurai.
3. Saluva Mangu received the title ‘Parapakshi Saluva’.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Kampana led the conquest, while General Saluva Mangu killed the Sultan and received the title ‘Parapakshi Saluva’.
accepted.tq: Test a conquest through its date, commander and associated title.
accepted.sec: Bukka I - southern conquest and its literary record (author), foreign embassy

accepted.s: Who wrote Madhura Vijayam?
accepted.x: Madhura Vijayam, a Sanskrit work describing the Madurai conquest, was written by Gangadevi, the wife of Kumara Kampana.
accepted.tq: Author–work recall with nearby literary distractors.
accepted.sec: Bukka I - southern conquest and its literary record (author), foreign embassy

accepted.s: Madhura Vijayam is a work in which language?
accepted.x: Madhura Vijayam was composed in Sanskrit by Gangadevi.
accepted.tq: Confusable author–language discrimination.
accepted.sec: Bukka I - southern conquest and its literary record (author), foreign embassy

accepted.s: Bukka I sent an embassy to the Ming emperor of China in which year?
accepted.x: Bukka I sent an embassy to the Ming emperor in 1374.
accepted.tq: Direct year recall using four distinct chronological values.
accepted.sec: Bukka I - southern conquest and its literary record (author), foreign embassy

accepted.s: Which agrahara was granted to the Telugu poet Nachana Somana?
accepted.x: Nachana Somana was granted the agrahara of Penchikaladinne. He was the author of Uttara Harivamsam.
accepted.tq: Direct place–person association.
accepted.sec: Bukka I - southern conquest and its literary record (author), foreign embassy

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Devaraya II’s military policy is correct?
1. He enrolled 10,000 Muslim soldiers.
2. Muslims received jagirs and a mosque.
3. He kept a Quran near his throne.
4. He improved cavalry and archery.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements describe Devaraya II’s army reforms and accommodation of Muslim soldiers.
accepted.tq: Use the complete military-policy cluster rather than an isolated reform.
accepted.sec: Devaraya II - army reforms, foreign visitors, titles

accepted.s:
Which of the following observations is associated with Abdur Razzaq’s account of Vijayanagara?
1. Open diamond bazaars
2. Three hundred ports
3. Taxation of prostitution
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Abdur Razzaq described the open diamond bazaars, the large number of ports and the taxation of prostitution.
accepted.tq: Cluster the distinctive details of one foreign traveller’s account.
accepted.sec: Devaraya II - army reforms, foreign visitors, titles

accepted.s: Which statement best resolves the association of Nicolo Conti with the Vijayanagara rulers?
o: He visited under Devaraya I, while some examination references associate him with Devaraya II.
He visited only during the reign of Bukka I and never during the Sangama period.
He visited Vijayanagara after the Talikota battle.
He was a Persian envoy of Shah Rukh in 1443.
accepted.x: Nicolo Conti’s visit is dated 1420–21, during Devaraya I, although an APPSC association places him under Devaraya II. He was an Italian traveller, not Abdur Razzaq.
accepted.tq: Resolve a close visitor–reign confusion through the date and nationality.
accepted.sec: Devaraya II - army reforms, foreign visitors, titles

accepted.s: Which of the following titles was NOT associated with Devaraya II?
accepted.x: Purva-Paschima Samudradhipati was the title of Harihara I. Devaraya II was known as Gajabetekara, Praudha Devaraya and Ilanti Raikonda.
accepted.tq: Find the title belonging to a different ruler.
accepted.sec: Devaraya II - army reforms, foreign visitors, titles

accepted.s: What does the title ‘Gajabetekara’ signify?
accepted.x: Gajabetekara means elephant hunter and was a title of Devaraya II.
accepted.tq: Translate the ruler’s title rather than merely identifying it.
accepted.sec: Devaraya II - army reforms, foreign visitors, titles

accepted.s:
Which of the following achievements is associated with Devaraya II?
1. Annexation of Kondaveedu in 1424
2. Collection of tribute from Sri Lanka through Lakkanna Dandanayaka
3. Repulsion of the Gajapatis, recorded in the Draksharama inscription of 1444
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Devaraya II annexed Kondaveedu, received Sri Lankan tribute through Lakkanna Dandanayaka and repelled the Gajapatis, as recorded at Draksharama.
accepted.tq: Link ruler, date, inscription and military achievement.
accepted.sec: Devaraya II - army reforms, foreign visitors, titles

accepted.s: Lakkanna Dandanayaka was associated with which title in the context of Devaraya II’s Sri Lankan policy?
accepted.x: Lakkanna Dandanayaka, who obtained tribute from Sri Lanka, was associated with the title ‘Dakshina Samudradhipati’.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a military officer’s title from royal titles.
accepted.sec: Devaraya II - army reforms, foreign visitors, titles

accepted.s: Srinatha received kanakabhishekam in the court of Devaraya II after defeating whom?
accepted.x: Srinatha received kanakabhishekam after defeating Gauda Dindima in the court of Devaraya II.
accepted.tq: Match the literary contest with the correct opponent.
accepted.sec: Devaraya II - army reforms, foreign visitors, titles

accepted.s: Which work is attributed to Devaraya II?
accepted.x: Mahanataka Sudhanidhi is attributed to Devaraya II. The other works are associated with Gangadevi, Nachana Somana and Irugappa respectively.
accepted.tq: Author–work discrimination among Sangama literary works.
accepted.sec: Devaraya II - army reforms, foreign visitors, titles

accepted.s: Vijayanagar, meaning the ‘City of Victory’, stood on the _____ bank of the Tungabhadra.
accepted.x: Vijayanagar stood on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra.
accepted.tq: Direct geographical-location recall.
accepted.sec: Capital city - river setting, present ruins site, irrigation works on the Tungabhadra → ruler

accepted.s: The ruins of Vijayanagar are located at which present-day site?
accepted.x: The ruins of Vijayanagar are located at Hampi.
accepted.tq: Ancient capital–present archaeological site association.
accepted.sec: Capital city - river setting, present ruins site, irrigation works on the Tungabhadra → ruler

accepted.s: Who built a dam across the Tungabhadra and arranged canals to carry water to the capital?
accepted.x: Devaraya I built a dam across the Tungabhadra and canals to carry water to Vijayanagar.
accepted.tq: Identify the ruler responsible for a specific public-works project.
accepted.sec: Capital city - river setting, present ruins site, irrigation works on the Tungabhadra → ruler

accepted.s: The Porumamilla inscription records the construction of which irrigation work?
accepted.x: The Porumamilla inscription, associated with Bhaskara Mantri, records the construction of the Porumamilla tank.
accepted.tq: Inscription–public work matching.
accepted.sec: Capital city - river setting, present ruins site, irrigation works on the Tungabhadra → ruler

accepted.s: After the battle of Talikota, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire was shifted in which sequence?
accepted.x: After Talikota, the capital moved from Hampi to Penukonda and subsequently to Chandragiri; both later capitals were in present-day Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Follow the first and second capital shifts in sequence.
accepted.sec: Capital city - river setting, present ruins site, irrigation works on the Tungabhadra → ruler

accepted.s: Saluva Narasimha was originally the lord of which place?
accepted.x: Saluva Narasimha was the lord of Chandragiri. His clan traced its origin to Kalyana.
accepted.tq: Direct home-base recall for a usurping ruler.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - home base, seizure of the Sangama throne, contemporary of Annamacharya, Gajapati and Bahmani wars

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the background of Saluva Narasimha is correct?
1. His clan came from Kalyana.
2. His ancestor Saluva Mangu served Kumara Kampana.
3. He was a ruler of the Tuluva dynasty.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Saluva clan came from Kalyana and Saluva Mangu served Kumara Kampana. Saluva Narasimha belonged to the Saluva dynasty, not the Tuluva dynasty.
accepted.tq: Reject the dynasty substitution while retaining the correct lineage facts.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - home base, seizure of the Sangama throne, contemporary of Annamacharya, Gajapati and Bahmani wars

accepted.s: Saluva Narasimha seized the Sangama throne in 1485 with the assistance of whom?
accepted.x: In 1485, Saluva Narasimha expelled Praudha Raya with the help of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka.
accepted.tq: Identify the associate in a dynastic usurpation.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - home base, seizure of the Sangama throne, contemporary of Annamacharya, Gajapati and Bahmani wars

accepted.s: The seizure of the Vijayanagara throne by Saluva Narasimha in 1485 is known as the:
accepted.x: Saluva Narasimha’s seizure of the throne in 1485 is called the First Usurpation.
accepted.tq: Direct event–term association.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - home base, seizure of the Sangama throne, contemporary of Annamacharya, Gajapati and Bahmani wars

accepted.s: Annamacharya, born in 1408 and deceased in 1503, was a contemporary of which ruler?
accepted.x: Annamacharya (1408–1503) was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha and is also placed in his court.
accepted.tq: Use overlapping life dates to identify the contemporary ruler.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - home base, seizure of the Sangama throne, contemporary of Annamacharya, Gajapati and Bahmani wars

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Saluva Narasimha’s wars is correct?
1. He drove the Gajapatis out by 1470 and held territory up to the Godavari.
2. He took the Machilipatnam area.
3. He repelled a Bahmani raid on Kanchi in 1481.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements describe the military achievements of Saluva Narasimha.
accepted.tq: Combine the ruler’s eastern, coastal and Bahmani campaigns.
accepted.sec: Saluva Narasimha - home base, seizure of the Sangama throne, contemporary of Annamacharya, Gajapati and Bahmani wars

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Jaimini Bharatam was written by Pillalamarri Pinaveerabhadra and dedicated to Saluva Narasimha. Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam.
accepted.tq: Detect the swapped author–work pair.
